blocks.content:
The CBI Director is appointed by the Central Government on the recommendation of a high-level committee consisting of:
• Prime Minister – Chairperson
• Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha
• Chief Justice of India (or a Supreme Court Judge nominated by the CJI)
The Director has a fixed tenure of 2 years, ensuring operational independence.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The CBI Director is appointed by the Central Government upon the recommendation of a three-member high-level committee.
The selection committee is chaired by the Prime Minister and includes the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha and the Chief Justice of India (or a Supreme Court Judge nominated by the CJI).
To ensure operational independence, the Director is guaranteed a fixed tenure of 2 years.
The composition of the recommendation committee consists of the Prime Minister (Chairperson), Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, and CJI/SC Judge.
The statutory tenure for the CBI Director is strictly fixed at 2 years.

blocks.content: The Director has a fixed tenure of **2 years**, ensuring operational independence.
